plan: This auction structure mirrors a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and I exit when the clock reaches my sealed bid. Bidding my true value is a dominant strategy here—bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding lower risks losing an item I could have profitably won. With no prior history to adjust for, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my value of $13.

This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by exit points on the clock. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy - it ensures you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and lose when it doesn't (avoiding losses). With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $15.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point in the ascending clock is determined by my sealed bid. Bidding my true value is a dominant strategy here—if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price above my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $47 to maximize expected profit.
